events.title: pip first released
events.summary: Ian Bicking released pip on October 28, 2008 — the [Python] package installer that replaced easy_install for most developers.
events.about: pip installs packages from PyPI with `pip install requests`, records versions in `requirements.txt`, and supports virtual environments. It became the standard way [Python] projects manage dependencies — Django, Flask, data science stacks, and ML pipelines all start with pip. The PyPA now maintains it.

narrative.whyChosen: pip made [Python] dependency management predictable after the frustrations of easy_install.
narrative.whyImportant: It established requirements files and PyPI as the default [Python] packaging workflow.
narrative.problemSolved: [Python] lacked a simple, reliable installer that handled uninstalls and version pinning well.

events.title: T-Mobile G1 released
events.summary: T-Mobile began selling the HTC Dream (T-Mobile G1) on October 22, 2008 — the first commercially available [Android] smartphone.
events.about: The G1 shipped with [Android] 1.0, a slide-out keyboard, and the [Android] Market for apps. It proved Google's open handset strategy could reach retail shelves — paving the way for Samsung, [Pixel], and billions of [Android] devices. Developers got a second native mobile platform beside iOS.

narrative.whyChosen: The G1 was the first phone to bring [Android] from announcement to consumers.
narrative.whyImportant: It validated [Android] as a real competitor to the iPhone and launched the dual-platform mobile era.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] needed a shipping reference device to attract developers and carrier partners.

events.title: Bitcoin whitepaper published
events.summary: Satoshi Nakamoto published "Bitcoin: A [Peer-to-Peer] Electronic Cash System" on October 31, 2008 — proposing a decentralized ledger secured by proof-of-work.
events.about: The paper described blocks chained by hashes, a difficulty-adjusted mining race, and incentives for honest nodes — without a central bank. Bitcoin launched open-source software in January 2009 and spawned blockchains, smart contracts, and a decade of debate about energy, regulation, and trustless systems.

narrative.whyChosen: The Bitcoin whitepaper introduced blockchain consensus to mainstream technical discourse.
narrative.whyImportant: It inspired cryptocurrencies, DeFi experiments, and new models of distributed trust.
narrative.problemSolved: Digital cash needed a way to prevent double-spending without a trusted intermediary.
